title: Adapter capability encoding and fallback sketch
content:
Purpose:
Quick, messy brain-dump for how a local/on-device adapter should advertise capabilities to the Redwood runtime and how the platform should pick fallbacks when an advertised capability is missing or degraded. Focus is on actionable API shape sketches, config examples, a few heuristics, and open questions.

Context / why this exists:
- We need a compact, versionable capability descriptor so hosted/Dedicated/Private control planes can reason about request routing and fallbacks without requiring exact model binaries to be present.
- Local adapters (edge modules, sidecars) will vary widely: quantized vs float, GPU vs CPU, memory caps, missing ops, degraded throughput. We must capture this succinctly and let RBW (router) make decisions.

Goals (informal):
- Small surface area: a capability map + optional runtime profile + dynamic health hooks.
- Backwards compatible: default conservative semantics.
- Enable automatic routing policies: prefer same-capability, fallback to degraded but acceptable, or rewrite requests for smaller context/precision.
- Make fallbacks explicit and auditable for SRE and product (so we can explain why a request served a different model).

Top-level API sketch (human-friendly):
- adapter_id: string (stable id for this adapter instance / package)
- version: semver-like string (major indicates breaking capability change)
- announced_capabilities: list of capability tokens (see below)
- resource_profile: light numeric hints (memory_mb, vram_mb, cpu_cores_est)
- quality_profile: optional scores (p50_latency_ms, token_quality_est 0..1)
- runtime_flags: list (e.g., supports_kv_cache, supports_streaming)
- fallback_rules: ordered list of fallback entries (policy DSL)
- health_endpoint: optional URI for runtime probe

Capability token examples (canonical strings, avoid long JSON):
- text-gen:streaming:true/false (streaming support)
- text-gen:precision:int8 / fp16 / fp32
- embeddings:dim:1536
- reranker:cross-encoder / bi-encoder
- kvcache:yes / partial / no
- max_seq:4096 (or 0 for unknown)
- persistent-context:yes/no

Note: tokens must be machine-parseable by control plane. We should avoid ad-hoc free text.

Example: adapter descriptor (YAML-ish for readability)

adapter_id: com.redwood.edge.adapter.t3
version: 0.3.1
announced_capabilities:
  - text-gen:precision:int8
  - text-gen:streaming:true
  - embeddings:dim:1024
  - kvcache:partial
  - max_seq:2048
resource_profile:
  memory_mb: 4096
  vram_mb: 0
  cpu_cores_est: 4
quality_profile:
  p50_latency_ms: 120
  token_quality_est: 0.86
runtime_flags:
  - supports_delta_patching
  - supports_prewarming

fallback_rules:
  - when: missing_capability(text-gen:precision:int8)
    prefer: text-gen:precision:fp16
    rewrite_policy: reduce_batch_size
    max_extra_latency_ms: 100
  - when: degraded_latency(p50 > 500)
    prefer: route_to_hosted
    notify: infra-oncall

health_endpoint: http://localhost:2200/adapter/health

Heuristic examples and how control plane uses them:
- Preference ordering: exact capability match > same-family different precision > remote-hosted equivalent > fail.
- Cost-aware: If adapter advertises token_quality_est < 0.75 and hosted model quality_est > 0.9, prefer hosted even if latency slightly higher.
- Resource-aware fallback: If request requires max_seq > adapter.max_seq, first attempt request rewriting (chunking or truncation) if caller allows, else fallback to remote model.
- Streaming containment: If adapter supports streaming:false but can buffer up to X tokens, the router can convert streaming -> buffered with an estimated added latency.

Fallback policy DSL (mini-spec):
- when: predicate (missing_capability(x), degraded_latency(p50 > N), memory_exceeded, supports_flag_missing)
- prefer: capability-token | route_to: (hosted|dedicated|private)
- rewrite_policy: none | reduce_batch_size | truncate_context | progressive_prefetch
- max_extra_latency_ms: int
- notify: list of alert targets (optional)

Telemetry and auditing hints:
- The adapter descriptor should include "discovery_time" and an ephemeral "last_health_ts"; the router logs the exact decision with: selected_path, why_chosen (predicate matched), metric_estimates used (latency, quality delta).
- Store decision provenance for 30 days by default.

ASCII diagram (very rough):

Caller ---> Router (control-plane) ---> match capabilities? ---> yes ---> Local Adapter (serve)
                           | no
                           v
                       apply fallback rules
                           | rewrite_request?
                           v
                   Route to hosted / dedicated / alternative

Open questions / TODOs (also for review):
- How to version capability tokens? (registry? Git-backed canonical list?) Suggestion: start with a small canonical set maintained in repo and require major version bump for breaking changes.
- Should adapters optionally provide a small verification test (mini-eval) on startup that returns a canned embedding or generation to validate quality_est? Pros: dynamic quality. Cons: privacy/compute cost.
- Is there a need for signed adapter descriptors (for on-prem security)? Possibly integrate with KMS/HSM signing.
- How do we express partial capabilities precisely (e.g., kvcache:partial meaning only prefix caching)? Need finer granularity.
- UX: how to surface to customers when fallback happened (in Console + per-request headers).

Implementation sketch (server side):
- Agent that consumes adapter descriptors from discovery (mDNS / control-plane registration) and normalizes tokens into internal Capability object.
- Router step: filter adapters by required capability set, score remaining by cost * (1 - quality_delta) + latency_penalty, then apply fallback_rules if empty set.
- Fallback evaluation engine: simple boolean predicate evaluator + rewrite orchestrator (rewrite policies are pluggable modules).

Immediate next actions (for me):
- (A) Draft canonical capability token list in repo (small set, iterate). Link: github PR above.
- (B) PoC: local adapter process that serves a descriptor JSON and health endpoint. Try route behavior with a simulated router agent.
- (C) Review with SRE for telemetry provenance requirements.

Notes to self:
- Keep these tokens small and composable. Avoid embedding too many numeric heuristics in string tokens; use resource_profile for that.
- When in doubt, fail conservative (i.e., prefer remote hosted model) unless an adapter explicitly claims high-quality and low latency.

End of sketch.
